messages.content: Organizer update on Philadelphia: both the Tuesday 2:30 funder roundtable and all Wednesday sessions are definitely at Loews. The block expires in three days. Can you re-run Loews vs. the Hampton before I hold anything? I’m weighing the hot July walk with materials against the lower rate and breakfast.
Yes. I’ll compare the full lodging picture, not just the nightly rate. Can you confirm the current refundable rates you’re seeing for July 21-23, one room, one adult?
Loews block is $239/night before tax, refundable until 72 hours out. Hampton Center City-Convention Center is $189/night refundable, breakfast included. Two nights. No car.

Here’s the clean comparison: | Hotel | Est. lodging total | Meeting logistics | Breakfast/room practicality | Dinner/no-car access | Trade-off | | Loews block | About $556 after tax, before breakfast | Same building; no July walk with materials; easiest for early Wednesday registration | Coffee maker listed; fridge/usable mini-fridge should be confirmed; breakfast not included | On-site restaurant plus easy nearby options | About $116 more than Hampton before breakfast, but very defensible as the event hotel | | Hampton CC-Convention Center | About $440 after tax | Roughly 10-12 minute walk to Loews, or short rideshare | Breakfast included; standard rooms generally list coffee maker and mini-fridge | Reading Terminal/Chinatown options nearby, but some hours vary | Better value, but the walk and materials add friction |
Can you look harder at the room amenities piece? I don’t want to be chasing coffee before registration, and I may need a fridge for snacks.

Hampton is stronger on that point: the standard king/queen room descriptions list an in-room coffee maker and mini-fridge. Loews lists in-room coffee/tea setup, but the refrigerator wording can mean either a mini-fridge or a stocked refreshment cooler, so I would add a booking note asking for a usable empty mini-fridge.
Would the Hampton walk be silly on Wednesday? Registration opens at 7:45, and I may have a small folder box.

Not silly, but it is the main downside. In mild weather with a tote, Hampton is fine. In late July with a folder box and a 7:45 registration, I’d budget a short rideshare that morning rather than walking. That narrows the real savings a little and adds one more moving part.
Tuesday dinner matters too. I’ll probably be done with the roundtable and not want to go hunting.

Loews wins for the low-effort Tuesday night: on-site dining, lobby-level fallback, and nearby Center City restaurants. Hampton still has good nearby food access, especially around Reading Terminal and Chinatown, but it is less seamless if you are tired or carrying materials back from the roundtable.
Reimbursement will accept the block if I justify it as the meeting hotel. I just don’t want it to look extravagant.

The justification is straightforward: official room block, sessions inside the hotel, early registration, no rental car, and materials to carry in July heat. The extra cost is not for luxury; it is buying schedule protection and eliminating local-transfer friction.
So would you hold Loews now instead of Hampton?

Yes. Hold the refundable Loews block before it expires. Put a reminder on the 72-hour cancellation deadline, and add notes for a quiet one-bed, non-smoking room plus a usable mini-fridge if available. Hampton is the budget winner, but with both meeting days inside Loews, the same-building convenience is worth the roughly $116 lodging premium.

messages.content: I held the Loews block. Can you refresh ORD-PHL flights for July 21-23 before I ticket? I need to leave Chicago Tuesday morning with enough time for bag drop before the 2:30 roundtable, and return Thursday after lunch without getting home late.

Best current choices: | Itinerary | Fare | Tuesday margin | Thursday return | Trade-off | | United nonstop | About $386 main cabin | ORD 8:55a-PHL 11:55a; likely at Loews around 12:45-1:00 | PHL 3:25p-ORD 4:45p; leave Loews around 1:10 | Cleanest timing, higher fare | | American nonstop | About $312 main cabin | ORD 10:05a-PHL 1:05p; hotel around 1:50-2:05 if smooth | PHL 5:05p-ORD 6:28p | Saves about $74, but outbound is tight and return stretches the day |
The American outbound getting me to the hotel near 2 makes me nervous. Could I pair the United outbound with the American return and save anything?

A split ticket prices around $348-$355 right now: United out at 8:55a, American back at 5:05p. It saves only about $30-$40 versus the all-United itinerary and adds split-carrier handling, so I would not choose it unless the United fare jumps.
What margin does the 3:25 United return leave if lunch ends around 12:45?

Comfortable but not wasteful. If you leave Loews around 1:10, a rideshare should put you at PHL about 1:40, giving roughly 1 hour 45 minutes before departure. If lunch slips past 1:15, then the later American return becomes the safer fallback.
So the midafternoon United is worth the premium here?

Yes. It protects the Tuesday arrival, still leaves room for Thursday lunch, and gets you back to Chicago before dinner. The cheaper option is not enough cheaper to justify the tighter outbound and later return.
Please use the United main cabin option, no basic economy. Aisle seat if available, but timing matters more.

Use this to ticket: United main cabin, ORD-PHL Tuesday July 21, 8:55a-11:55a; PHL-ORD Thursday July 23, 3:25p-4:45p, about $386. Plan on a rideshare from Loews to PHL around 1:10 Thursday. Keep the later American return only as a backup if lunch is extended.
